avl_cl_tolerance.guards: AVL neutral point and roll rate: AVL reaches the requested lift coefficient; a larger miss is a defect of ours.
avl_cl_tolerance.source: AVL prints C_L with five decimals

avl_contour_margin.guards: AVL airfoil file: an airfoil point may lie this far outside the unit chord (rounding of a repanelled contour) before the file is refused.
avl_contour_margin.source: rounding of a contour whose x runs from 0 to 1

avl_control_echo_tolerance.guards: Roll rate: the control AVL echoes must be the commanded deflection.
avl_control_echo_tolerance.source: AVL prints the control with five decimals

avl_refinement_tolerance_mac.guards: Neutral point: the disagreement of the declared and the refined AVL mesh, in mean chords, above which the value is declared not converged.

avl_roll_branch_tolerance.guards: Roll rate: the trimmed roll rate must agree with the linearised one from the stability derivatives to this relative difference, else AVL's Newton iteration landed on a spurious branch.
avl_roll_branch_tolerance.source: a numerical sanity check of the solver, no domain threshold: the nonlinearity measured on the fleet is 0.2-0.4 %, a spurious branch is off by a factor of about 3 (#1211)

avl_roll_moment_tolerance.guards: Roll rate: the stability-axis rolling moment left by the steady roll; a larger residual is a defect of ours.
avl_roll_moment_tolerance.source: AVL prints the stability-axis rolling moment with five decimals

avl_roll_print_floor.guards: Roll rate: added to the branch check as the print resolution of AVL's p'b/2V (five decimals) and its derivatives (six).
avl_roll_print_floor.source: AVL prints p'b/2V with five and the derivatives with six decimals

avl_roll_refinement_tolerance.guards: Roll rate: the relative disagreement of the declared and the refined AVL mesh above which the roll rate is declared not converged.
avl_roll_refinement_tolerance.source: maintainer, #1211 D8: fixed before any measurement; the agreement asked of the independent template reference

opt_active_bound_fraction.guards: Optimisation: an optimum within this fraction of the range of a variable lies on its bound, and a value on a bound is no optimum (ADR 0020), so it is refused.
opt_active_bound_fraction.source: IPOPT's bound push keeps an interior optimum a few 1e-8 of the range from its bound; 1e-6 separates it from a bound the solver reached

opt_alpha_margin_deg.guards: Angle comparisons of the stall checks and the half-step sweep grid: two angles closer than this are the same sample of the lattice.
opt_alpha_margin_deg.source: float noise of an angle that is a multiple of a quarter degree; many orders below the sweep step

opt_flap_rib_gap.guards: Flap: the spanwise offset of the second section written at a rib where the flap state changes. AeroBuildup divides by the width of a strip, so two sections at the same place give NaN (measured: RV-7 with landing flaps).
opt_flap_rib_gap.source: the smallest offset that keeps the strip well defined (measured: finite results at 1e-6 m, NaN at 0); a millionth of a metre moves the next strip's start by far less than the geometry's own tolerance

opt_fuselage_area_tolerance.guards: Fuselage section: the relative disagreement of the cross-section area of the equivalent symmetric section and of the section with two exponents, at which the bracketed search for the equivalent exponent stops.
opt_fuselage_area_tolerance.source: a margin over floating-point noise of the gamma-function area (about 1e-16): the search is a bisection, so the tolerance costs only a few extra halvings; a looser value would leave a visible area error in the drag build-up

opt_hinge_floor.guards: Control effectiveness: added to the hinge position so a hinge at exactly 0 does not raise 0 to a fractional power.
opt_hinge_floor.source: the smallest margin that keeps the power well defined at a hinge position of 0

opt_peak_tolerance.guards: Stall speed, postcondition: C_L,max may fall short of the sampled first peak by this much; both are samples of one curve, so it only absorbs numerical noise.
opt_peak_tolerance.source: float noise between two samples of one sweep

opt_probe_tolerance.guards: Stall speed, postcondition: the relative disagreement allowed between V_S and the closed form with the polar's C_L at alpha_S.
opt_probe_tolerance.source: IPOPT's default convergence tolerance is 1e-8 on the scaled constraint, so 1e-6 leaves two decades for the scaling and the sweep's float rounding

opt_zero_span.guards: Angle interpolation: two lift-coefficient samples closer than this count as equal, so no division by their difference.
opt_zero_span.source: a margin over floating-point noise of C_L, which is of order 1

altitude.source: the reference point of the International Standard Atmosphere (U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976: geopotential altitude 0 at mean sea level, where rho = 1.225 kg/m^3); a starting value (maintainer 2026-10-25, #1258): the designer sets the field altitude, e.g. 500 m

approach-speed-margin-target.regime: transport rule taken as the lower bound: at low wing loading and low speed a gust changes the angle of attack and load factor more (Scholz Wing Design §7.3), so RC needs at least this margin; a larger RC margin has no source
approach-speed-margin-target.source: Lennon, Basics of R/C Model Aircraft Design, Ch. 20 (FAR 23 reasoning, scaled); CS 25.125 as transport-category reference

battery-specific-energy.regime: RC LiPo packs, pack level (wiring, balance lead, shrink included); the cell-level figure of the cited RC-Network value (152.8 Wh/kg) is higher by construction
battery-specific-energy.source: maintainer, 2026-10-25 (#1235): pack level, a round value inside 128–159 Wh/kg; that band comes from the catalogue's ten 'Generic LiPo' entries, which are placeholder data, not manufacturer datasheets — no published pack value is cited yet

cell-voltage-nominal.regime: regime-independent: a property of the cell chemistry, not of the flow; a mid-discharge value, so the rated mAh times it is the energy at the manufacturer's test rate; the caller overrides it for another chemistry
cell-voltage-nominal.source: SkyRC, "RC Battery Lineup: Voltage Ranges by Chemistry Types", SkyRC Blog, 2024-12-26 (https://blog.skyrc.com/rc-battery-lineup-voltage-ranges-by-chemistry-types/): nominal per cell LiPo 3.7 V (LiHV 3.8 V, LiFe 3.2 V, Li-Ion 3.6 V, NiMH 1.2 V); the default is the LiPo value, the fallback of a battery with neither cell_voltage_v nor chemistry (maintainer 2026-10-25, #1245); a battery with a chemistry takes that chemistry's value from the same source

gravity.source: standard gravity, CGPM 1901 / U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976

limit-load-factor.regime: RC/UAV models: far above the transport and FAR 23 values (2.5–6 g), inside the measured 6–19 g; the designer overrides it per airplane
limit-load-factor.source: maintainer, 2026-10-25 (canon review of maneuvering-speed): 10 g instead of the former 3; measured loads on models are 6–19 g (spar sizing); to be replaced by a mission table with its structure-mass consequence (#1242)

load-factor.source: definition of the load factor n = L/W (as stated in max-mass-structure); straight level flight means L = W

motor-efficiency.regime: RC brushless motors (the source's subject); at P_max copper loss grows with I², so the efficiency lies below the peak band and the lower bound fits
motor-efficiency.source: Roxxy Motoren-Fibel, Ch. 3: efficiency band 75–85 %; the lower bound, because route A applies it at P_max, above the peak-efficiency point; the fallback of a motor without a published efficiency_pct (maintainer 2026-10-25, #1290)

stall-break-fraction.regime: a measurement convention on the computed polar, not a flight regime: clearly above solver noise (a 1-3 % drop can be one non-monotone sample) and close enough to the peak that the 360 deg blend of the polar does not dominate; applies at the stall Reynolds number of the polar
stall-break-fraction.source: maintainer decision 2026-10-24 (#1219); no published value (Anderson, Sadraey, Lennon describe the stall break qualitatively and quantify it nowhere)

static-margin-target.source: Drela, Basic Aircraft Design Rules (MIT 16.Unified Lab 11, 2009), Eq. (2): S.M. = 0.05...0.15; maintainer 2026-10-25 (#1258): 0.10 as the starting value, the designer sets the target per airplane

tail-efficiency.regime: not checked at RC Reynolds number: the wing wake is thicker at low Re, by an amount no source quantifies; Lennon's model-scale value is used instead of the full-scale 0.85–0.95. The designer overrides it per airplane
tail-efficiency.source: Lennon, Basics of R/C Model Aircraft Design (1996) Ch. 7/8: conventional tail near the wing wake 0.65 (T-tail 0.9, in the wake 0.4); Sadraey, Aircraft Design (2013) Eq. 6.28 §6.2.1: 0.85–0.95 conventional, 1 T-tail, full-scale; maintainer decision 2026-10-24 (#1205); basis start (a starting value; Lennon gives the value), maintainer 2026-10-25

takeoff-speed-margin-target.regime: rise-off-ground without wheel brakes has no decision-speed logic; Sadraey's ground roll rotates at about 1.1 V_s (§4.3.4.2 Eq. 4.76); hand launch: no source
takeoff-speed-margin-target.source: Sadraey, Aircraft Design (2013), §4.3.4: V_TO = 1.1–1.3 V_s (lower edge)

touchdown-speed-margin-target.regime: RC models flare to near V_min and have no wheel brakes, so the low end of the band applies; the old 1.2 (Lennon) is a landing speed with a safety margin, which approach 1.3 covers. Maintainer decision 2026-10-17
touchdown-speed-margin-target.source: Sadraey, Aircraft Design (2013), §4.3.2: take-off and landing speeds are typically 1.1–1.3 V_s; §9.3.10: flare to minimum speed

n_load.source: definition of the load factor n = L/W (as stated in max-mass-structure); straight level flight means L = W
definition of the load factor n = L/W (as stated in max-mass-structure); straight level flight means L = W
definition of the load factor n = L/W (as stated in max-mass-structure); straight level flight means L = W
definition of the load factor n = L/W (as stated in max-mass-structure); straight level flight means L = W
definition of the load factor n = L/W (as stated in max-mass-structure); straight level flight means L = W
definition of the load factor n = L/W (as stated in max-mass-structure); inverted level flight means L = −W

aerobuildup-no-deflected-device.criterion: AeroBuildup is given the flaps of a configuration as deflected contours (#1212; the stall-speed applications takeoff and landing) and the roll command as an aileron surface; any other deflected control device is refused rather than computed as the clean airplane.

aerosandbox-fuselage-shape.criterion: AeroSandbox has no mirrored body: a mirrored fuselage is refused rather than approximated. It has one shape exponent per fuselage section: a section with n_lower different from n is not refused but mapped to the equivalent symmetric section of the same width, height and centre and equal cross-section area, declared per section as the practice warning fuselage_section_equivalent (#1307, ADR 0020).

airfoil-positive-thickness.criterion: An airfoil has a maximum thickness greater than zero: a NACA designation with a thickness above 00, a contour whose upper surface lies above its lower surface somewhere.

airfoil-resolvable.criterion: An airfoil is a NACA 4-digit designation or inline coordinates (the kernel loads no files); a contour has at least min_contour_points points and starts and ends at the trailing edge, the largest x (Selig order).

min_contour_points.source: three points are the least that enclose an area; the first and last point being the trailing edge makes the order Selig

avl-array-limit.criterion: AVL's vortex array has a fixed size; a mesh that overflows it is refused (avl_array_limit) and a refined check that overflows is declared, never silently dropped.

avl-mesh-layout.criterion: The AVL mesh drives the roll devices of the main wing only: a roll device on another surface (unsupported_layout) is refused. The continuity of the hinge line is the rule hinge-line-continuity.

avl-no-deflected-device.criterion: AVL runs the clean airplane: the kernel writes no CONTROL, so a deflected control device is refused rather than computed as the clean airplane.

avl-roll-rate-validity.criterion: AVL is linear in the deflection: the AVL world of the roll rate is used while |p b / 2V| is at most max_roll_rate_coefficient; beyond it the world is declared outside its validity and dropped from the interval (A11).

max_roll_rate_coefficient.regime: RC/UAV: model roll rates stay inside the primer's range at approach speed (BRYAN 0.29, JAGUAR 0.28 at 20 deg are beyond it, which is why the AVL world is dropped there); the limit is a property of AVL's linearisation, not of the flow regime
max_roll_rate_coefficient.source: AVL primer (Avl/avl_doc.txt:121-141): -0.10 < pb/2V < 0.10 is the practical limit for roll rates, beyond which results should be interpreted with caution; adopted for the AVL world by the maintainer on #1243, 2026-10-25

control-surface-needs-device.criterion: A control surface is given only on a section that has a trailing-edge device: the kernel takes role and hinge from the device.

finite-numbers.criterion: Every number of the geometry that the kernel reads is finite (no NaN, no infinity).

flap-deflection-with-flaps.criterion: An airplane that has flaps is given the flap deflection of the configuration; the kernel takes no default.

flap-model-validity.criterion: A flap is the rotated contour behind its hinge, evaluated by NeuralFoil (a plain, single-element flap; maintainer 2026-10-26, #1212). The result of stall-speed (take-off and landing applications) and of roll-rate (approach) is declared outside the model's trusted range when NeuralFoil's analysis_confidence of a section at the solution is below min_confidence (flap_confidence_low), and when a flap deflection is above max_flap_deflection (flap_deflection_beyond_validity). The value is computed and returned with the declaration, never withheld.

max_flap_deflection.regime: transport and general-aviation material for the separation angle, not checked at model Reynolds number (ADR 0028); the adopted value is deliberately below it
max_flap_deflection.source: plain-flap separation above about 40 deg (Scholz ch. 8 / Sadraey 5.12.2), earlier at low Re; 30 deg keeps a margin; adopted by the maintainer 2026-10-26, #1212

min_confidence.regime: RC/UAV: measured at chord Reynolds numbers 1e5 and 3e5, inside the band of ADR 0028
min_confidence.source: the app's existing low-confidence flag for NeuralFoil polars, app/settings.py low_re_low_confidence_flag = 0.85 ('Low analysis confidence - validate with XFoil'); one threshold for one concept; adopted by the maintainer 2026-10-26, #1212. The kernel must not import app/ (E8), so the value is stated twice: a later change of either must change both. Measured on RV-7 (NACA 23013.5, Re 1e5, hinge 0.75): flap 15 deg gives confidence of at least 0.93 at the section, 30 deg 0.35 to 0.8

hinge-line-continuity.criterion: Two driven segments of a roll device that meet at a rib (their positions in y closer than join_tolerance) have the same hinge position there: AVL holds one hinge position per section. The same distance decides that a station of a device end and the rib it was read from are one rib.

join_tolerance.regime: regime-independent: a statement about the geometry document, not about the flow
join_tolerance.source: a numerical identity of two positions of one rib; no published source (maintainer 2026-10-26, #1299: a domain limit that stays an overridable rule parameter)

isa-altitude-range.criterion: The altitude lies inside the range of AeroSandbox's International Standard Atmosphere (the range is the tool's own, read from it).

main-wing-spanwise-extent.criterion: A wing of surface_type main_wing is inclined from the horizontal by less than max_inclination over its stored sections: arctan((max z - min z) / (max y - min y)) < max_inclination; a wing with no y-extent is a vertical surface and is refused. AeroSandbox would measure a vertical surface without complaint (a slant planform).

max_inclination.regime: regime-independent: a statement about the shape of the surface, not about the flow
max_inclination.source: adopted by the maintainer on 2026-10-25 (#1253); no published source. The dihedral of a real main wing stays far below it, even a strong V (10-15 deg), while a fin or a V-tail typed main_wing has y-extent <= z-extent

minimum-sections.criterion: A wing and a fuselage have at least min_sections sections: a surface needs a root and a tip.

min_sections.source: a lofted surface is defined by at least two sections

neutral-point-layout.criterion: The neutral point is defined for one main wing with one horizontal tail (any fins and winglets); a tailless wing, a canard, a tandem wing and a V-tail are refused (#1206, #1207, #1208).

one-main-wing.criterion: The airplane has exactly required_main_wings wings of surface_type main_wing: its area, span and chord are the reference values.

required_main_wings.source: one reference wing per airplane; biplanes are out of v1 (ARCHITECTURE 8.5)

positive-lengths.criterion: Every chord, every fuselage semi-axis (zero allowed at an end section) and every fuselage shape exponent is greater than zero, and the leading-edge chain of a wing has a length greater than zero.

roll-device-on-mirrored-surface.criterion: A roll device (aileron, flaperon, elevon) sits on a mirrored surface and has a hinge position (rel_chord_root); the tool's default hinge is never used.

sections-monotone-in-y.criterion: The sections of a mirrored surface run from the root outwards without doubling back in y (a fin: in z): a planform that doubles back would be counted twice.

segment-details-not-on-last-section.criterion: The last section of a wing carries no trailing-edge device, spar list or turbulator: it ends the wing and has no segment outboard of it.

static-margin-probe-agreement.criterion: The static margin from the moment slope (the probe) agrees with the target static margin to within agreement_tolerance, in fractions of the mean aerodynamic chord; a larger deviation is reported, never averaged.

agreement_tolerance.regime: regime-independent as a statement about agreement; the value rests on the spread of the methods in the RC/UAV regime
agreement_tolerance.source: maintainer 2026-10-25: 5 % MAC. Reasoning: the neutral-point worlds spread 3-6 % MAC (textbook against AVL, BRYAN and JAGUAR), plus the declared probe bias (AeroBuildup has no wing-tail downwash)

surface-type-required.criterion: Every wing has a surface_type; the kernel never infers one from the planform (D9).

directions.explanation: Design quantities: a target turned into a construction quantity (O1).
directions.label: Design

disciplines.explanation: Forces, the polar, stall, and the speeds set as a margin over the stall speed.
disciplines.label: Aerodynamics

disciplines.explanation: Unpowered performance: best glide, minimum sink, sink rate, glide distance, crow.
disciplines.label: Glide performance

disciplines.explanation: Thrust, climb, top speed, sustained turn, endurance and range on the battery, and their sweeps over the mass.
disciplines.label: Powered performance

disciplines.explanation: Static stability and trim about the pitch axis: neutral point, static margin, the CG for a target margin, the CG envelope.
disciplines.label: Longitudinal stability and trim

disciplines.explanation: Lateral-directional stability and roll control: dihedral and weathercock effect, spiral, fin volume, roll rate and the aileron deflection a roll target needs.
disciplines.label: Lateral-directional stability and control

disciplines.explanation: Manoeuvre and dive speeds, break load factors, spanwise loads and hinge moments.
disciplines.label: Structure and loads

groups.explanation: Density, viscosity and speed of sound at the altitude (ISA).
groups.label: Air state

groups.explanation: Reference area, span, mean aerodynamic chord, aspect ratio.
groups.label: Geometry references

groups.explanation: The airplane in its take-off and landing configuration.
groups.label: Configurations

groups.explanation: The powertrain: motor, battery and propeller.
groups.label: Powertrain

groups.explanation: Motor and propeller values from the catalogue, and the pack voltage they run on.
groups.label: Motor and propeller

groups.explanation: Battery capacity, mass and specific energy, and the predicted battery mass.
groups.label: Battery

groups.explanation: Lift, drag, dynamic pressure, the required lift coefficient and the lift-to-drag ratio at a state.
groups.label: Forces and state

groups.explanation: The linear part of the lift curve: slope and zero-lift angle.
groups.label: Linear lift curve

groups.explanation: The stall: C_L,max, the stall angle of attack and the polar at the stall Reynolds number.
groups.label: Stall

groups.explanation: The parabola fitted to the solver polar (C_D0, Oswald e, k): display only, never an input to performance (ADR 0026).
groups.label: Fitted parabola (display)

modules.explanation: Targets that name an operating point or bound the envelope: the stall-speed margins of approach, touchdown and take-off, the cruise-speed target and the limit load factor.
modules.label: Envelope targets

modules.explanation: Targets a design entry turns into a construction quantity: the static-margin target, the stall-speed target and the roll-rate targets (O1).
modules.label: Design targets

modules.explanation: The airplane as built and its fitted components (motor, battery, propeller), with the references derived from them: geometry references, the take-off and landing configurations and the powertrain values. Cross-cutting: nearly every formula depends on it.
modules.label: Construction

modules.explanation: The take-off mass and the centre of gravity, inputs of the canon (A6), with the weight and the wing loading derived from them. Cross-cutting.
modules.label: Mass and balance

modules.explanation: Altitude and the physical constants, with the air state derived from them: density, viscosity and speed of sound. Cross-cutting.
modules.label: Atmosphere and constants

modules.explanation: Every device angle the caller sets: ailerons, elevator, rudder, flaps for take-off and landing, crow. The geometry stops are never read.
modules.label: Control deflections

modules.explanation: The free variables of a flight state: flight speed, angle of attack and load factor. Named points bind them instead.
modules.label: Operating point

modules.explanation: Defined values: measurement conventions with a default but no published source, adopted on the maintainer’s word. Every quantity that rests on one carries the ≈ mark.
modules.label: Defined values

points.explanation: C_L,max at n = 1 or −1, clean configuration.
points.label: Stall, clean

points.explanation: The take-off configuration and its speeds.
points.label: Take-off

points.explanation: The landing configuration and the approach at V_app = k_S · V_S0.
points.label: Landing / approach

points.explanation: V_md, the minimum-drag speed; also the reference point of static stability.
points.label: Best glide (V_md)

points.explanation: Only when a cruise-speed target is given.
points.label: Cruise target

points.explanation: A state the caller sets (V, α, n); no named point yet — a visible gap against A2.
points.label: Free operating point

points.explanation: Geometry or components only, no operating point.
points.label: No operating point

stages.explanation: The cross-cutting inputs turned into reference values: air state, geometry references, weight and wing loading, the take-off and landing configurations, the propulsion catalogue values.
stages.label: Derived references

stages.explanation: The polar independent of the operating point: lift and drag, the lift-curve slope, zero-lift angle, C_L,max, the fitted parabola.
stages.label: Aerodynamic model

stages.explanation: Where the named speeds are born: V_S0, V_S,TO, V_md, V_mp, V_app, V_TO, V_A. Every final result of a point depends on them.
stages.label: Named operating points

stages.explanation: The propeller at a flight speed: rotational speed, advance ratio, thrust coefficient.
stages.label: Propulsion state

stages.explanation: The neutral point and the positive break load factor, on which the stability and structure results build.
stages.label: Stability and structure
